column3: The Hebrew explicitly adds “all the people from the extremity.”
The Hebrew uses “know them” where BSB explains “have relations with them.”
“Have not known a man,” “good in your eyes,” and “the shadow of my roof” preserve the Hebrew images.
The Hebrew says “from small to great” where BSB has “young and old.”
The Hebrew repeatedly uses the singular “him,” including the LORD’s compassion toward him.
The commands are singular, addressing Lot individually, rather than “your lives.”
The Hebrew address is singular, “my lord.”
The Hebrew says “my soul may live” where BSB has “my life will be saved.”
The Hebrew uses the idiom “I have lifted your face” for granting his request.
The Hebrew places her “behind him” as she looks.
